title: Famine Lyall Commission
definition: The Lyall Commission (1898) was a British-appointed commission tasked with investigating the causes and management of the severe Indian famine of 1896-97, following the recommendations of the earlier Strachey Commission.
importanceInUpsc: UPSC frequently tests the evolution of British famine policy in India. The Lyall Commission represents the transition from 'laissez-faire' relief to more structured, albeit colonial-centric, administrative intervention.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Famine Lyall Commission.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Understanding of British Land Revenue Systems
